slides.title: What quitting p*rn feels like [[week by week]] in No Nut November.
slides.sub: You're in week 2. Here's what's coming — so it doesn't catch you off guard.

slides.title: The [[easy]] start — then the wave
slides.body: Motivation is high. Then around day 4–5, many people describe a sudden wave of p*rn urges. If you made it through, the hardest surprise is behind you.

slides.title: The [[restless]] week
slides.body: Irritable, bored, can't sleep, thinking about p*rn more than you expected. This is where most people quit NNN. You're in it right now.

slides.title: The [[flat]] week
slides.body: Low energy, low drive, "is this even working?" Many describe this flat phase before things improve. Don't mistake it for failure.

slides.title: The [[clear]] week
slides.body: Many people report more focus, more energy and fewer p*rn urges by the last week. Everyone's different — but the people who reach it rarely regret it.
slides.note: What week are you in? Comment 1, 2, 3 or 4 👇

carousels.name: You failed No Nut November. Now what?

slides.title: You failed No Nut November by Day 5. [[Stop pretending it doesn't matter.]]
slides.sub: Laughing it off is easier than admitting p*rn has more control than you thought.

slides.title: "It was just a [[joke]] anyway."
slides.body: No. You tried to go 30 days without p*rn and couldn't make 5. That's not a joke. That's information.

slides.title: Stop [[waiting]] for December
slides.body: "I'll try again next year." That's 12 more months of p*rn running your nights. You don't need November to start. You need today.

slides.title: Restart [[right now]]
slides.body: Day 1 can be November 11 just as easily as November 1. The challenge ends on the 30th. Your p*rn addiction doesn't care about the calendar.

slides.title: Your [[restart]] plan
items: Today is Day 1. No waiting.
Block p*rn on every device tonight.
Find what broke you on Day 5 — time, place, mood.
Aim for 19 days, then keep going past Nov 30.
slides.note: Restarting today? Comment "DAY 1" and hold yourself to it 👇

carousels.name: 9 signs you're more addicted to p*rn than you think

slides.title: 9 signs you're more addicted to p*rn [[than you think.]]
slides.sub: If you hit 4 or more, it's time to stop calling it "just a habit."

slides.title: Signs [[1–3]]
items: You plan your day around when you'll be alone.
You open p*rn even when you're not in the mood — just out of habit.
You have tabs or folders you'd die if anyone saw.

slides.title: Signs [[4–6]]
items: You use p*rn to fall asleep most nights.
You get irritable when you can't access it.
You've watched p*rn somewhere risky — work, class, family home.

slides.title: Signs [[7–9]]
items: Real intimacy feels like more effort than it's worth.
You've lied about how much p*rn you watch.
You've tried to quit 3+ times and couldn't.

slides.title: Counted [[4+]]?
slides.body: Then this isn't a phase or a quirk. It's p*rn addiction — and it's treatable. Naming it honestly is the first real step.
slides.note: How many did you count? Save this and come back in 30 days 🔖

carousels.name: Only 4-10% ever get help for p*rn addiction

slides.title: Most people struggling with p*rn [[never ask for help.]]
slides.sub: What the biggest international study found.

slides.title: Almost [[nobody]] seeks help
slides.body: In the International Sex Survey (Bőthe et al., 2024), only 4–10% of people with problematic p*rn use had ever sought treatment.

slides.title: Why people [[stay quiet]]
slides.body: Shame. Fear of judgment. Thinking "it's not that bad." Believing they should handle p*rn alone. Silence feels safer — but it keeps you stuck.

slides.title: You're [[not]] the only one
slides.body: The same study of 42 countries found men reported the highest levels of problematic p*rn use. Millions are fighting this quietly.

slides.title: Be in the [[4–10%]]
items: Tell one person you trust about your p*rn use.
Talk to a therapist or doctor — it's their job.
Join a support group — anonymous is fine.
Use tools that keep you accountable.

carousels.name: Week 2 of No Nut November is the hardest

slides.title: Week 2 of NNN is where [[most p*rn quitters break.]]
slides.sub: 5 reasons it's so hard — and how to get through it.

slides.title: Why it's [[hard]]
items: The novelty is gone. Day 11 doesn't feel exciting.
The p*rn urges are louder than week 1.
Everyone else already quit — so it feels pointless.

slides.title: And [[worse]]
items: You start bargaining: "I've done 10 days, one p*rn session won't matter."
You haven't felt the benefits yet — so you doubt it's working.

slides.title: Here's the [[truth]]
slides.body: The bargaining voice gets loudest right before p*rn urges start to ease. Week 2 is the toll you pay to reach week 3.

slides.title: Survive [[week 2]]
items: Expect it to be hard — that's normal, not failure.
Remove all p*rn access tonight.
Fill your evenings — train, see people, go out.
Count down: 19 days left.
slides.note: Still in? Comment "DAY 11" so others know they're not alone 👇
